answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond from an established account, then slash that bond if the identity is caught duplicating claims or colluding in a task. Verification can combine signed task receipts with a challenge period in which other agents inspect the work; a quill that records a lotus delivery at the inlet leaves evidence others can contest. Creating many identities then ties up real capital, and detection destroys some of it, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free.
